factors: Nine material claims, including unreplicated operator-scale and quality figures
Consequential inference-service, data governance and hardware recommendation
complexity.rationale: A performance and infrastructure source needs an extended argument, explicit measurement denominators, competing service designs and a falsifiable deployment test.

sourceMap.rationale: The scope section separates inspectable offline release code from missing serving components and avoids claiming a successful build.
The architecture section compares the public release boundary with the operator description of internal deployment scale.
The denominator section connects plotted device scale and acceptance accounting to a narrower measurement claim.
The quality section attributes exact reference scores and names dataset, judging and output limitations.
The control section labels cluster token volume and revenue illustration as operator claims and asks for local hardware inventory.

sourceCoverage.rationale: Five mapped source sections cover release scope, architecture, performance denominator, reference quality and operator scale. The remaining sections are explicit original analysis or proposed tests.

supportingArgument.rationale: The code tree, hardware support, parallelism features and documented component results receive their strongest plausible engineering interpretation before the critique.

evidenceRoles.rationale: Pinned first-party code and docs show what is released and asserted; SGLang and vLLM supply methodology only; no outside performance replication is claimed.

counterargument.rationale: The essay acknowledges that real code, sweep scripts and narrowly optimized hardware can make DeepInfer valuable for matching workloads, while mature servers are credible comparators.

tradeoffs.rationale: It examines cache reuse versus real traffic, accepted-token throughput versus latency, offline engine versus missing control planes, narrow accelerators versus deployment effort.

falsifiability.rationale: The proposed test pins code and model, inventories hardware, compares complete services on matched traces and states outcomes that would change the recommendation.

originalSynthesis.rationale: GhostMesh distinguishes engine performance, service operation and human outcome ownership; the conclusion does not restate a maintainer benchmark as a universal verdict.

performance.rationale: The analysis identifies four-versus-64-GPU plots, shared-prefix defaults, full draft-acceptance accounting, omitted TTFT and queue tails, and the need for matched quality.

economics.rationale: The first-party US$38 per GPU-hour revenue example is not called profit; total service cost, occupancy, operating labor and network cost remain unknown.

threatGovernance.rationale: The essay identifies KV retention and isolation, model and dependency supply chain, egress, routing authority, recovery and synthetic failure testing without alleging an incident.

decisionRationale: Tony qualitatively accepted the exact previewed article after independent source and copy review found no remaining defect. The direct authenticated GitHub acceptance marker and a separate exact-head production release decision are still pending.
